AK.agency: Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development, Division of Workers' Compensation
AK.threshold_note: The Act requires each employer having one or more employees in Alaska to obtain workers' compensation insurance, unless approved as a self-insurer (agency page, last updated 2026).

AK.agriculture_rule: Agency lists harvest help and similar part-time or transient help as an exception; it tells employers to call the division about specific situations
AK.counts_owners: Since 1 Aug 2019 sole proprietors, partners, LLC members with at least 10% ownership, and executive officers of for-profit corporations with at least 10% ownership are exempt from insuring themselves. Employees, including family members and friends, must still be covered.
AK.penalty_summary: Stop work order for failing to insure; $1,000 per day for violating a stop work order; penalties of $10 to $1,000 per employee for each day worked during a lapse in coverage (agency employer guide). Special Investigations Unit page says up to $1,000 per employee per day uninsured.
AK.statute_citation: Alaska Workers' Compensation Act, AS 23.30 (AS 23.30.025 and AS 23.30.230 cited on agency pages)

CA.agency: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation (DWC)
CA.threshold_note: DWC FAQ: all California employers must provide workers' compensation under Labor Code 3700; if a business employs one or more employees, it must satisfy the law. Fact sheet (Sept 2024): coverage required even with just one employee; benefits cover part-time employees.
CA.construction_rule: Same one-employee rule. CSLB: licensed contractors must file proof of insurance or a signed exemption certifying no employees. C-8 concrete, C-20 HVAC, C-22 asbestos abatement, C-39 roofing and C-61/D-49 tree service contractors must carry coverage whether or not they have employees.
CA.counts_owners: Executive officers and directors of corporations must be covered unless the corporation is fully owned by its directors and officers, in which case they may elect to be excluded. A sole proprietor may choose to be covered by endorsement but is not required to be.
CA.owner_exemption_form: No state form for corporate officers; election to exclude is made through the insurance policy. Contractors with no employees file a signed workers' compensation exemption with CSLB.
CA.penalty_summary: Labor Code 3700.5: misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not less than $10,000 or up to one year in county jail, or both. State penalties of up to $100,000 against illegally uninsured employers. Employer is liable for all injury costs and can be sued civilly by the injured employee.
CA.withholding_note: California EDD registers UI, employment training tax, disability insurance and personal income tax withholding in one payroll tax account

FL.agency: Florida Department of Financial Services, Division of Workers' Compensation
FL.threshold_note: Non-construction: employers with four (4) or more employees, including business owners who are corporate officers or LLC members, must have coverage. Non-construction sole proprietors and partners in a partnership are not employees unless they elect coverage and file form DWC-251.
FL.construction_rule: Employers with one or more employees, including owners who are corporate officers or LLC members, must have coverage
FL.agriculture_rule: Employers with six (6) regular employees and/or twelve (12) seasonal workers who work more than 30 days during a season and/or more than 45 days in the same calendar year
FL.counts_owners: Corporate officers and LLC members count as employees toward the threshold but can apply for an exemption. Construction: no more than three officers or members of an affiliated group may be exempt; at least 10% ownership attested. Non-construction corporations: no limit on officers; LLCs: up to 10 members, at least 10% ownership.
FL.owner_exemption_form: Notice of Election to be Exempt, online application to the Division of Workers' Compensation; construction $50 fee, non-construction no fee; applicant must sign personally; validity period not found in pages read
FL.penalty_summary: Stop-Work Order requiring the employer to cease all business operations, plus a statutory penalty equal to 2 times the premium the employer would have paid in the preceding year (up to 2 years). Concealing payroll can bring criminal charges. Release needs proof of compliance and a minimum $1,000 down payment on the penalty with a payment plan (agency brochure).

GA.agency: Georgia State Board of Workers' Compensation
GA.threshold_note: If you regularly employ three or more persons in your Georgia business, you are required to provide workers' compensation benefits. GA.counts_owners: Corporate officers and LLC members are employees and count toward the three-employee rule even if they waive coverage. GA.owner_exemption_form: Form WC-10 (officer or member waiver of coverage), signed and filed with the insurance carrier; up to five officers or members may waive; fee and validity not stated
GA.penalty_summary: Civil penalties of up to $5,000 per violation and a year in prison (Board coverage verification page).

IA.agency: Iowa Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing (DIAL), Workers' Compensation Division
IA.threshold_note: Agency page: Iowa law requires most employers to have workers' compensation liability insurance or register as self-insured; covers employees in most employment relationships. No headcount is stated on the page; one employee is inferred.
IA.agriculture_rule: Limited exemptions apply to those employed in agriculture or by a relative; exemptions are described as complex and the agency says to consult an attorney. Some exemptions depend on annual earnings from the employer being under $1,500.
IA.counts_owners: Proprietors, LLC members, LLP members and partners may file a nonelection of coverage. Up to four corporate officers (president, vice president, secretary, treasurer) may file a rejection of coverage; other employees cannot. Neither can be required as a condition of employment.
IA.owner_exemption_form: Nonelection of Coverage (proprietors, LLC and LLP members, partners) and Rejection of Coverage (up to four corporate officers), both filed online with DIAL if there is no policy, with two unaffiliated witnesses; if a policy exists, attach the written nonelection to the policy. No fee or fixed validity stated; can be terminated any time.
IA.penalty_summary: Employers without required coverage may face criminal or civil penalties and lose workers' comp protection, so they can be sued in tort for full damages. Iowa Code 87.14A: willful and knowing violation is a class D felony.
IA.statute_citation: Iowa Code 87.14A (insurance required); Iowa Code 87.22 (exclusion of officers, proprietors, members, partners)

Uninsured employer loses Act protections and can be sued in civil court (Section 4(d)).
